topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the introductory framing and pedagogical objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer etiology: genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish core concepts of cancer development by exploring intrinsic mutations, the microenvironment, environmental risk factors, and geographic epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious agents and oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how biological pathogens promote carcinogenesis, highlighting the specific etiology and translocation mechanism of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Direct and metabolically activated chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and various chemical mutagens cause DNA damage, adduct formation, and mutations either directly or following xenobiotic metabolism.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, physiological susceptibility, and carcinogenesis mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address non-mutagenic aspects of carcinogenesis, including promotion mechanisms, developmental windows of vulnerability, and an integrated summary of carcinogenic pathways.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogens and assessing risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the experimental, epidemiological, and genomic tools used to identify carcinogens alongside practical considerations in weighing exposure risks against benefits.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and summary
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks and final summary framing for the lecture.
